_meta: Three model responses that each try to emit a tool call, used to show that a harness must decide whether to execute a tool call from the response's finish_reason (why generation stopped), not from whether the emitted arguments happen to parse as JSON -- because a response cut off by the max-token limit produces incomplete arguments, and sometimes those incomplete arguments are still valid JSON, so a harness that trusts a successful parse will execute a call the model never finished specifying. When a model emits a tool call and generation stops because the call is complete, the finish_reason is a completion reason (tool_calls or stop) and the arguments are whole. When generation stops because it hit the max-token limit, the finish_reason is length and the arguments are whatever had been written so far -- truncated. Truncation usually leaves the JSON malformed (an unterminated string), and a naive parse then fails. But truncation can also land on a point where the partial JSON is accidentally well-formed -- the model wrote the first field and a closing brace's worth of structure by luck -- and then json.loads succeeds and returns arguments that are missing every field the model had not reached yet. Executing that call runs a dangerous, wrong operation (a delete scoped to /data instead of /data/tmp/cache, a write to the wrong path) that the model never actually requested. The fix is to gate execution on finish_reason: a response with finish_reason length is an unfinished turn and its tool call must not be executed -- the harness continues the generation or errors, but never guesses the missing arguments. r1 is a complete call, r2 is truncated into invalid JSON, r3 is truncated but accidentally valid; each response's text, finish_reason, and the arguments the model actually intended are the fixture, and whether each harness executes it, and with what arguments, is computed. Stdlib only.
